entries.title: Ocean Climate Teleconnection Drivers (Pacific RONI, Indian Ocean DMI & Western-V)
entries.summary: Harmonised multi-decadal monthly and seasonal time series of primary equatorial ocean-atmosphere climate teleconnection drivers governing Kenyan rainfall: NOAA CPC Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) for Pacific ENSO state; NOAA CPC / HadISST Dipole Mode Index (DMI) for Indian Ocean Dipole state; and Funk et al. Western-V SST index for MAM Long Rains teleconnections. Standardised and compiled into analysis-ready parquet tables (1950 to present).

producer.organization: NOAA Climate Prediction Center
Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
producer.name: Peter Steward

citation.text: NOAA Climate Prediction Center; Funk, C.; Steward, P. (2026) Ocean Climate Teleconnection Drivers (RONI, DMI, Western-V), 1950-2026. African Agriculture Adaptation Atlas / NOAA CPC.

caveats: Attribution: "Data provided by NOAA Climate Prediction Center (CPC) and compiled for the African Agriculture Adaptation Atlas (AAAA)." RELATIVE OCEANIC NINO INDEX (RONI) OVER RAW NINO 3.4. CPC computes RONI by subtracting the tropical-mean (20S-20N) SST anomaly from the Nino 3.4 anomaly. This detrending removes secular tropical ocean warming (~+0.6 degC since 1950) that otherwise causes historical cool baselines to register as artificial permanent El Nino conditions. Always use RONI for multi-decadal analogue selection. INDIAN OCEAN DIPOLE (IOD) DOMINANCE IN SHORT RAINS. The DMI is the primary physical forcing of Kenyan rainfall variability during the October-December (OND) Short Rains. Warm ENSO and positive IOD co-occur frequently but can decouple; off-diagonal states (El Nino + negative IOD) produce subdued anomalies. SEASONAL ASYMMETRY AND LONG RAINS (MAM) DECOUPLING. Pacific ENSO indices exhibit weak correlation with Kenyan rainfall during the March-May (MAM) Long Rains (r ~ 0.08). The Western-V index captures western Pacific warm pool gradients that govern convective subsidence over the Horn of Africa, providing independent predictive skill where ENSO fails. Z-SCORE STANDARDIZATION REQUIREMENT. Pacific SST anomalies (~0.5-2.5 degC) and regional rainfall anomalies exhibit a 10.6:1 variance distortion ratio. Multi-driver analogue selection must use z-score standardisation across all driver dimensions to ensure equal physical weighting.

avoid.use: Deterministic point-forecasts of county rainfall from ocean index values alone.
avoid.reason: Ocean drivers alter conditional probability distributions; local weather is mediated by topography and synoptic meteorology.
avoid.use_instead: Ensemble probabilistic scenarios combined with official KMSA statutory outlooks.

intended_uses: Selecting historical analogue seasons for Kenyan seasonal outlooks.
Evaluating conditional probability distributions of rainfall anomalies.
Quantifying seasonal teleconnection asymmetry between OND and MAM.

entries.title: JRC / GloFAS Return-Period River Flood Hazard (Global)
entries.summary: Modelled global riverine flood hazard from the JRC / GloFAS Global Flood Maps (CEMS-GLOFAS v2.1.2): inundation depth for seven return periods, 10 to 500 years, at 3 arc-seconds, as a static baseline climatology. Published as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs with internal overviews on Source Cooperative, which is the canonical read location. The Adaptation Atlas additionally holds a provisional Kenya crop of the same data. Within the KE-ENSO Explorer this is the MODELLED flood-prone baseline complementing the OBSERVED Copernicus GFM extent (record kenya-flood-gfm): JRC answers "how flood-prone at magnitude X", GFM answers "where and when it actually flooded".

caveats: FEDERATED TO THE CLOUD-OPTIMIZED UPSTREAM (2026-09-18, following review on cdh-catalog#32). The full global product is already published as COGs with internal overviews under CC-BY-4.0 on Source Cooperative, at the same seven return periods and the same 3 arc-second resolution as the Atlas crop. entries.title: Kenya Observed Flood Extent (Copernicus GFM, Sentinel-1)
entries.summary: Observed flood extent for Kenya from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service Global Flood Monitoring (GFM) product, which classifies flooding from every Sentinel-1 SAR acquisition (ensemble of the DLR, TU Wien and LIST algorithms; permanent and reference water excluded). Delivered as ~111 m aggregates built directly from the 20 m SAR tiles: a monthly flood-occurrence layer with its valid-observation count, a rolling 3-month (seasonal) layer aligned to the KE-ENSO Explorer precipitation seasons, and a full-record history (occurrence frequency and ever-flooded footprint), 2018 to present. Replaces the MODIS Global Flood Database (ended 2018) with a cloud-penetrating, continuously updated SAR record. The 20 m per-acquisition archive is not materialised here (16,000+ acquisitions); it can be re-pulled from the EODC STAC on demand.

caveats: Attribution required: "Contains modified Copernicus Emergency Management Service information [year]". Pixel coding of the flooded layers: 0 = not flooded, 1 = flooded, 255 = not observed (SAR gap or excluded) - 255 is absence of observation, NOT dry; the nobs layer gives the count of valid observations so no-flood is distinguishable from no-observation. Seasonal windows are named by the initials of their months and labelled by the year of their FIRST month (DJF_2018 = Dec 2018 to Feb 2019), so NDJ and DJF exist for 2018 to 2024 only. This differs from the CHIRPS seasonal record (africa-precipitation-monthly-seasonal), which labels NDJ and DJF by the year the window ends; align on those two windows with care. A ~7-year record measures recent observed flood occurrence, not return-period magnitude.

entries.title: Kenya Flood x Exposure, Per-Sub-County Tables
entries.summary: Pre-computed flood x exposure statistics for Kenya's 290 IEBC sub-counties (admin 2), as three small Parquet tables the KE-ENSO Explorer reads directly (DuckDB-WASM) instead of intersecting heavy rasters and vectors in the browser. Two hazard products - Copernicus GFM observed flood (per season x year, 2018 to 2025) and JRC modelled return-period flood hazard - are each crossed with population (WorldPop constrained 100 m grid, levelled to the official KNBS county totals), classified roads and the electricity transmission grid (length exposed) and health and school facilities (count exposed); a third table holds the per-sub-county denominators. Tables carry no geometry: join on adm2_pcode to the boundary record kenya-admin-codab.

producer.organization: Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
producer.name: Peter Steward

citation.text: Steward, P. (2026) Kenya flood x exposure per-sub-county tables, Africa Agriculture Adaptation Atlas (KE-ENSO Explorer). Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT.

caveats: Derived aggregate statistics; no input geometry is redistributed. Please attribute the inputs: Copernicus GFM and JRC Global Flood Maps (Copernicus / European Commission), WorldPop constrained population (CC-BY-4.0), OpenStreetMap roads and HOTOSM facilities ((c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), KPLC grid (CC0-1.0, energydata.info), IEBC COD-AB boundaries (OCHA, CC-BY-3.0-IGO). In the GFM table, observed_pct is the SAR-observed share of the sub-county in that season: low values mean sparse observation, not absence of flooding. Road and grid kilometres are cell-resolution approximations (in-cell line length within flooded cells). Every table also carries adm1_pcode, adm1_name and adm2_name label columns. POPULATION METHOD (issue #28), stated in full. Headcounts are NOT raw gridded pixel sums. Every published sub-county population is built as three explicit factors, each published as its own column:
pop_adm2 = pop_adm2_grid x pop_scale_census x pop_growth_county
(1) pop_adm2_grid - the 100 m gridded pixel sum, which supplies the SHARE of the county's people
living in that sub-county, and nothing else.
(2) pop_scale_census = census county total / gridded county total - replaces the LEVEL of the
gridded surface with the enumerated KNBS 2019 census, county by county. The gridded surfaces
run about 17 per cent above the census (WorldPop constrained ~55.2 M, GRID3 ~55.9 M, census
47,564,296), so this factor is ~0.855 nationally but spans 0.324-1.394 across individual
counties (measured on the published grid, 2026-09-17): WorldPop exceeds the census by up to
threefold in some counties and falls below it in others. Any aggregate therefore moves by a
weighted mix of county factors, not by the national one - flood-exposed population sits mostly
in low-factor counties, so the GFM exposed total fell about 35 per cent where the national
denominator fell 14 per cent. No time component.
(3) pop_growth_county = target county total / census county total - the county's proportional
CHANGE OVER TIME, from the KNBS Vol XVI projections (record
kenya-population-knbs-projections). Exactly 1.0 when the denominator is the census itself.

County is the only level where any of this is defensible: COD-AB adm2 is 290 IEBC constituencies while the census reports 345 KNBS sub-counties, and only 183 names match (record kenya-population-knbs-census); KNBS does not project below county at all. FIXED-SHARE ASSUMPTION. Each sub-county's share of its county is held constant at the gridded 2020 distribution, so every sub-county in a county moves by exactly that county's percentage change. Sub-county-specific growth is NOT represented: a fast-urbanising sub-county and a depopulating one in the same county grow at the same rate here. Growth does vary between counties - the 2025 factors span 1.03 to 1.15 - but not within one. YEAR MATCHING (the published default from 2026-09-17). The GFM table records OBSERVED floods and carries a year, so a single fixed denominator is wrong in one direction or the other: the 2019 census undercounts a 2024 flood by roughly 9 per cent, and a 2025 projection overcounts a 2018 one by a similar margin. Each GFM row is therefore levelled against ITS OWN year's county population, and pop_year records which year was used. Years the KNBS projections cover (2020 onward) use them; 2018 and 2019 fall back to the enumerated census, because nothing official projects backwards from the 2020 base and inventing a figure would be worse than stating the fallback. Consequence for consumers: pop_source VARIES BY ROW in the GFM table - "knbs-census-2019" for 2018-2019 and "knbs-projection-<year>" thereafter - so do not read one value and assume it applies to the file. The JRC table is a return-period hazard with no event year, and the totals table is a static denominator, so both take a single stated reference year (pop_year, same on every row). TWO DEFINITIONS OF THE GROWTH FACTOR, recorded in pop_method:
county-growth-from-<base year> - pop_growth_county = projection(year) / projection(base year,
2020). The enumerated census remains the level and KNBS supplies only the shape of change;
national 2025 lands near 51.96 M because the ~2.6 per cent step KNBS puts between census night
(August 2019) and its own 2020 base is deliberately not imported.
county-level - pop_growth_county = projection(year) / census(2019), so the county total IS the
published official projection and national 2025 is 53,330,978 - the figure a Kenyan
counterpart would quote - at the cost of superseding the census anchor with the KNBS base-level
revision.

processing.description: Zonal intersect of the flood masks with the sub-county polygons, the population raster, rasterised per-cell road and grid line length, and facility points. Attribution is given as a courtesy though CC0 does not require it. The supporting evidence gathered earlier still stands: Evidence for the licence, recorded because knbs.or.ke itself carries no terms page (the terms-and-conditions URL 404s and the footer asserts "All Rights Reserved"), which is misleading: (1) KNBS operates an Open License Agreement covering its Open Data Platform, granting a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use, copy, modify, publish, adapt, distribute and create derivative works for commercial and non-commercial purposes, subject to attribution. Use county totals plus a gridded within-county share for any adm2 denominator; do not join this table to COD-AB sub-counties on name. Male + Female (47,562,772) falls 1,524 short of the published Total because KNBS suppresses the intersex count below national level; the residual is carried as pop_intersex. The age-and-sex table comes from HDX cod-ps-ken (UNFPA, CC-BY-3.0-IGO), which redistributes the same census (Volume III) with adm1 p-codes attached. DO NOT SWITCH THE SOURCE TO THE HDX COPY of the sub-county table, despite its cleaner licence status: that copy is defective. It carries 346 rows to this source's 345 because the Tharaka-Nithi COUNTY total (393,177) appears as if it were a sub-county, inflating the national figure to 47,957,473 against the published 47,564,296. This ingest uses the knbs.or.ke workbook, which reconciles exactly. (It also spells Kutulo as "Kotulo"; same value, harmless.)

caveats: MIXED-STATUS RECORD - READ BEFORE REUSE (decision 2026-09-18). The source documents are KNBS publications, linked here and not hosted by the Atlas. Three DERIVED parquet tables were published to digital-atlas BEFORE the licence was correctly established; they reproduce KNBS figures, so they are NOT open data. They are documented here deliberately: leaving a public object undocumented is worse than describing its true status. They must not be treated as open data, and this record must NOT be submitted to cdh-catalog, until written permission exists from KNBS (info@knbs.or.ke / directorgeneral@knbs.or.ke). Permission request is deferred as of 2026-09-18, so this state persists by decision, not by oversight. HOW THE ATLAS USES THIS WITHOUT REDISTRIBUTING IT. The exposure chain applies projections as a dimensionless growth ratio on a census anchor, never as absolute published values: R/observational/_population_helpers.R, POP_METHOD=county-growth (the default at 7_zonal_exposure.R:138 and 7b_relevel_exposure_pop.R:64) computes projection_county(year) / projection_county(2020) and multiplies the CC0 census count by it, so no published artifact reproduces a KNBS projection. The alternative POP_METHOD=county-level reproduces the official county total exactly and must NOT be used for anything published. Ratios are read from the Summary Report, which carries no rights reservation, rather than from Volume XVI.

LICENCE - CORRECTED 2026-09-18, READ BEFORE REUSE OR REDISTRIBUTION. This record previously claimed the KNBS Open License Agreement. That was WRONG. Volume XVI was read directly on 2026-09-18 and its copyright page states: "(c) 2022 Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. All rights reserved. No part of this publication may be reproduced, distributed, or transmitted in any form or by any means ... without the prior written permission of the Bureau." The KNBS Open License Agreement is scoped to data published on the KNBS Open Data Platform and does not reach a PDF published on knbs.or.ke, and a search of HDX on 2026-09-18 found NO licensed mirror of these projections anywhere - the UNFPA COD-PS product (cod-ps-ken, CC-BY-3.0-IGO) carries the 2019 census only and contains no projections, so there is no openly licensed substitute. CONSEQUENCE. Extracting these figures for analysis is ordinary research use. REDISTRIBUTING them, including as the derived parquet files this record points at, needs written permission from KNBS (info@knbs.or.ke / directorgeneral@knbs.or.ke, the addresses given in the report). Until that permission exists this record must NOT be submitted to cdh-catalog, and the published derivatives should be treated as pending clearance rather than as open data. Tracked in hazards_prototype issue 33. This constraint does NOT apply to the census counts - record kenya-population-knbs-census is CC0-1.0, released without restriction by KNBS's own HDX account.

LICENCE EVIDENCE. Weaker footing than the census record, and the difference is worth stating. KNBS's Open License Agreement grants worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive rights to reuse, adapt, redistribute and create derivative works with attribution - but it is scoped to data published on the KNBS Open Data Platform, and Volume XVI is a PDF hosted on knbs.or.ke. Unlike the 2019 census tables, no licensed mirror of these projections exists anywhere (searched HDX, open.africa and the Kenya data portal, 2026-09-17): UNFPA's COD-PS covers the census, not Volume XVI. What is published here is a derived tabulation of figures printed in a public national statistical report, attributed, not a copy of the report. Confirm with KNBS before this record is contributed to cdh-catalog. Required attribution: "This product was adapted from the Statistical Office of Kenya's information, which is licensed under the KNBS Open License Agreement."

COUNTY ONLY. Volume XVI does not project below county - no sub-county name appears anywhere in the report - so this record stops at county. The KE-ENSO exposure tables (record kenya-flood-exposure-intersect) do carry sub-county figures for a projection year, and the way they get there is stated there in full: each sub-county's share of its county is held fixed at the gridded 2020 distribution and the whole county is moved by its own percentage change from this table (pop_growth_county), with the enumerated census supplying the level. That means no sub-county-specific growth is represented; growth varies between counties (2025 factors span 1.03 to 1.15) but is uniform within one. Anyone wanting genuine sub-county differentials needs a source that produces them - this one does not. YEAR COVERAGE IS UNEVEN. The report's annual panels cover 2020-2035; 2040 and 2045 appear only in the five-yearly milestone panel, so 2036-2039 and 2041-2044 are absent. TWO SOURCE DEFECTS, both handled and logged by the ingest rather than silently absorbed. (1) Busia 2030, age 80+, female reads 3,120 in the 2030-2035 panel against 5,799 in the two other panels that carry 2030; the printed row total (9,714) reconciles only with 5,799, so 5,799 is used. (2) Kiambu's 2026-2030 panel labels its open-ended top age group "80-84" where every other panel says "80+"; it is relabelled "80+", without which it would double-count against the overlapping panels. KNBS rounds each printed cell independently, so sums do not close exactly: age groups land within five people of the printed All Ages row, and the 47 counties sum to roughly 15 to 20 people below the national row in every year. The identical report is also hosted as ...-Analytical-Report-on-Population-Projections-Vol-XVI.pdf (2024/05, 32.9 MB); its extracted text is identical to the 2023/09 upload used here.

entries.title: MapSPAM 2020 Adaptation Atlas, Sub-Saharan Africa
entries.summary: Spatially disaggregated crop statistics for Sub-Saharan Africa: 42 crops across six production systems, harmonised to FAOSTAT country totals, as physical area, harvested area, production, yield and value of production. A regional adaptation of IFPRI's MapSPAM 2020 built for the Africa Agriculture Adaptation Atlas, supplementing the global release with national and sub-national sources. This is the crop-production basis of the Atlas exposure chain: every crop value-of- production layer, and through them the hazard-exposure product, is distributed across these production shares.

caveats: NOT THE SAME DATASET AS THE HUB'S `spam2020` RECORD, DESPITE THE NAME. That record describes IFPRI's GLOBAL MapSPAM 2020 v2r2, licensed CC-BY-SA-4.0 and published as zarr. This one is the Atlas's Sub-Saharan Africa adaptation, licensed CC-BY-4.0 and published as GeoTIFF. Different scope, different licence, different format, different DOI. Do not substitute one for the other, and note that the share-alike term on the global release does NOT reach the Atlas exposure chain, which consumes this product. THREE PROCESSING LEVELS, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. `raw` holds the released CSVs, one file per variable and technology code (P_TA, P_TH, P_TI and so on). `analysis-ready` holds rasterised GeoTIFFs. `atlas-harmonized` holds the Atlas value-of-production layers derived from them. The VoP chain reads `analysis-ready/variable=prod_t` and writes into `atlas-harmonized`. FILE NAMING DIFFERS BETWEEN LEVELS. The irrigated system is `irrigated` under `analysis-ready` and `irr` under `atlas-harmonized`. Anything templating a path across both levels must special-case it; the token values below are given per level for that reason. CURRENCY BASIS IS A KNOWN TRAP. Several value-of-production variables coexist - vop_intld15, vop_usd2015, vop_nominal-usd15, vop_nominal-usd21 - and they are NOT interchangeable. A past mismatch between the crop and livestock currency bases produced roughly a sevenfold error in cattle exposure. Constant international dollars (vop_intld15) is the Atlas standard; check the livestock counterpart is on the same basis before combining. Tracked as hazards_prototype issue 30. THREE OBJECTS ARE PUBLISHED UNDER A MALFORMED KEY. Directly beneath `region=ssa/` there are three parquet objects whose path reads `processing=atlas-harmonizedvariable=<name>.parquet`, missing the separator between the two hive fields: crop-livestock_all, vop_intld15-2021 and vop_nominal-usd-2021. entries.title: Kenya Acute Food Insecurity Phase Classification (IPC / KFSSG)
entries.summary: IPC Acute Food Insecurity phase classifications and population-in-phase tables for Kenya, produced twice a year by the Kenya Food Security Steering Group after the long-rains and short-rains assessments. A federated record - the Adaptation Atlas cites this analysis but does not host it.

producer.organization: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Global Partnership
Kenya Food Security Steering Group (KFSSG)
Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
producer.name: Peter Steward

citation.text: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) Global Partnership (2026) IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis, Kenya. IPC Global Support Unit, hosted by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

caveats: LICENCE CONFIRMED 2026-09-18, AND IT CONSTRAINS DOWNSTREAM USE. IPC states that all IPC results are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO. Two consequences that do not apply elsewhere in the Atlas stack: NON-COMMERCIAL, so IPC figures cannot travel into a commercially licensed or commercially used product; and SHARE-ALIKE, so any adapted work built on them must carry the same licence, which conflicts with the CC-BY-4.0 most Atlas products use. Citing IPC phases and linking out is unencumbered; folding them into a derived Atlas layer is not. The IPC Analysis Platform is hosted by FAO and governed by its terms of use. A PHASE IS A CLASSIFICATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Phases 1-5 come from an expert consensus process over converging evidence, so they are ordinal and are NOT comparable across analysis rounds in the way a measured index is: methodology, evidence base and analyst panel all change between rounds. Do not difference phases between rounds to derive a trend, and do not interpolate between analyses. Kenya analyses are conducted twice a year - long rains (July-August) and short rains (January-February) - and the IPC process is hosted within NDMA.

avoid.use: Differencing phases between analysis rounds to derive a trend.
avoid.reason: A phase is an expert-consensus classification over converging evidence, not a measurement. Methodology, evidence base and analyst panel all change between rounds, so the ordinal scale is not comparable across them.
avoid.use_instead: Compare the population-in-phase figures within a round, and treat each round as its own analysis.

avoid.use: Folding IPC phases into a derived Atlas product licensed CC-BY-4.0.
avoid.reason: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO is both non-commercial and share-alike, so the derived work would have to carry the same terms - incompatible with the rest of the Atlas stack.
avoid.use_instead: Cite the classification and link to IPC, or seek written permission from the IPC Global Support Unit.

avoid.use: Interpolating between analyses to get a monthly series.
avoid.reason: Kenya is analysed twice a year, after the long-rains and short-rains assessments; nothing is observed between.
avoid.use_instead: Use the analysis windows as published.

intended_uses: Placing a season's climate anomaly next to the food-security outcome that followed it, in the KE-ENSO Explorer.

entries.title: Kenya County Gender Data Sheets, 2025
entries.summary: Gender and social-inclusion indicators for all 47 Kenyan counties, published as one data sheet per county in October 2025. Indicators cover health and fertility, education, economic participation, political representation, disability and attitudes to intimate-partner violence, drawn largely from the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey, the 2019 census and the 2022 general election. A federated record - the Adaptation Atlas reads these sheets but does not host or redistribute them.

producer.organization: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS)
State Department for Gender and Affirmative Action, Ministry of Gender, Culture and Children Services
Council of Governors
UN Women (Women Count)
SDGs Kenya Forum
Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT
producer.name: Peter Steward

citation.text: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics; State Department for Gender and Affirmative Action; Council of Governors; UN Women (2025) County Gender Data Sheets, 2025. Kenya National Bureau of Statistics.

caveats: LICENCE - AN EXPLICIT WORKING ASSUMPTION, NOT A GRANT. No party has published terms for these sheets. The Atlas treats them as open pending evidence otherwise, a decision taken by the data owner on 2026-09-18 and recorded here so it is visible rather than implied: LicenseRef-KE-Gov- Statistics-Assumed-Open means "no rights stated, treated as open", NOT "the publishers granted an open licence". Anyone relying on these figures commercially should confirm with the publishers first. The evidence behind the assumption follows. Every page of a sheet was read and the raw PDF scanned: there is NO copyright notice, NO "all rights reserved" and NO ISBN. That is materially better footing than the KNBS census projections (record kenya-population-knbs-projections, whose Volume XVI reserves rights in terms) - but absence of a notice is NOT a grant, and copyright subsists automatically. Worse, there is no single party whose terms could be pointed at: these are a six-way co-publication. The KNBS Open License Agreement does NOT reach them, being scoped to data published on the KNBS Open Data Platform, while these are PDFs on knbs.or.ke - the same gap already established for Volume XVI. UN Women co-publishes under the Women Count programme and normally releases CC-BY-3.0-IGO, which is a signal and not a statement. Settle with UN Women Kenya or the State Department for Gender before anything derived from these is published. EDITION. The October 2025 set, all 47 county sheets, uploaded to knbs.or.ke in April and May 2026. Not the 2019 ten-county pilot, and not a mix. A static cross-section, not an ongoing series. SIZE. The Atlas extraction yields 1,578 rows: 35 indicator series across 24 stable codes, long format, county level only. VINTAGE IS NOT UNIFORM AND IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM THE SHEETS AS EXTRACTED. Indicators mix 2022 KDHS, 2019 census-derived figures and 2022 election results. The Atlas extraction strips any trailing year from indicator labels, so no per-indicator reference year survives in the derived table. Treating the whole table as "2022" is wrong for some indicators. BLANK IS NOT ZERO. The extraction serves a series only where at least 40 of 47 counties agree with the modal national value; non-matching county rows are dropped individually. So a served series can be silently missing up to seven counties, and a missing county-series is a parse or gate drop - NEVER an observed zero. Only 10 of 35 series reach all 47 counties; the worst is households with an elderly member at 40/47. Per-county row counts run 22-35. COVERAGE IS ASYMMETRIC WITHIN AN INDICATOR. One code can have 47 counties for male and 46 for female. Do not compute a sex ratio or a gender gap without checking both sides are present for that county. CHART-ONLY INDICATORS ARE ABSENT BY METHOD. Antenatal-visit and vaccination charts and internet usage are dropped by the gate. Their absence reflects the extraction, not the source. LABELS ARE NOT DEFINITIONS. The canonical label is the longest string seen across the 47 sheets and several remain truncated mid-sentence. Do not lift them into variable descriptions. COLUMN-ORDER FRAGILITY. Values are read Kenya-then-County from the printed header. A future edition that flips that header would swap every value silently; the coverage gate catches it only if the national column also becomes inconsistent.

avoid.use: Reading a missing county-series as a zero or as a low value.
avoid.reason: Series are gated at 40 of 47 counties and non-matching rows are dropped individually, so absence is a parse or gate artefact rather than an observation.
avoid.use_instead: Check per-series county coverage before mapping or ranking; only 10 of 35 series are complete.

avoid.use: Treating the table as a single reference year, such as 2022.
avoid.reason: The sheets mix KDHS 2022, 2019 census-derived and 2022 election vintages, and the extraction strips trailing years from labels, so no per-indicator year survives.
avoid.use_instead: Recover the reference year per indicator from the source sheet before making any temporal claim.

avoid.use: Computing a sex ratio or gender gap without checking both sides.
avoid.reason: Coverage is asymmetric within a code - one sex can have 47 counties and the other 46.
avoid.use_instead: Require both sexes present for that county, or drop the county from the comparison.

intended_uses: Gender and social-inclusion disaggregation of county-level exposure in the KE-ENSO Explorer.

assets.name: county-data-sheets
assets.description: 47 county gender data sheets, October 2025, one PDF per county, roughly 12 pages each. Linked, not hosted. Acquisition is NOT scripted in a public repository - the raw PDFs, the URL list and the download script sit on project OneDrive, so this dataset is reproducible by transform but not by fetch.

processing.description: KNBS, the State Department for Gender and Affirmative Action, the Council of Governors, UN Women (Women Count) and the SDGs Kenya Forum compile county indicators, largely from KDHS 2022, the 2019 census and the 2022 general election, and publish one PDF data sheet per county.

Deterministic text extraction from the 47 PDFs - pymupdf get_text("blocks"), two-column split on x0 < 320, sorted by page, column and y, keyed on the printed indicator code (^([A-E]\d{1,2})\s*[:.]), values read Kenya-then-County per the printed header, then gated: a county row is dropped where its extracted national reference value does not match the modal national value for that code and sub-series, and a series is served only where at least 40 of 47 counties survive. No language model touches a number, and nothing is transcribed by hand.

dimensions.name: county
dimensions.description: County name as printed on the sheet, 47 counties. The sheets carry names, not p-codes; any p-code is an Atlas-side addition mapped to IEBC COD-AB adm1 (record kenya-admin-codab).

dimensions.name: indicator_code
dimensions.description: Stable indicator code as printed (A3, B1, D10 and so on). The extraction keys on this code and never on label text - keying on labels fragmented a single indicator into 142 near-duplicate variants in an earlier attempt. 24 codes are served.

dimensions.name: sub
dimensions.description: Splits a code by sex, or by measure variant such as Gross against Net Attendance Ratio. 35 series across the 24 codes.

variables.name: county_value
variables.description: The county figure for that indicator series, as printed on the county sheet.

variables.name: kenya
variables.description: The national figure printed alongside the county figure. Also the gate key - a series is served only where at least 40 counties agree with the modal national value.
